title: Celebrity post backs up the feed
description: Every new post ID is pushed into every follower's cached feed list. A singer with 120 million followers posts during an awards show, and fan-out lag reaches 20 minutes. Friends' everyday posts get stuck behind that work too. What design change removes the celebrity-sized write spike?

options.text: Add a read replica to the follow store so workers can read follower lists faster.
options.explanation: Reading followers is not the bottleneck; the 120 million feed writes are, and they would still be queued ahead of everyone else's posts.

options.text: Switch everyone to fan-out on read so no writes are needed.
options.explanation: That removes the write spike but makes every feed load touch hundreds of authors, which breaks the read latency target for the far more common case.

options.text: Store the full post object in each feed list so readers skip hydration.
options.explanation: This increases the size of each of the 120 million writes and does nothing about the write amplification causing the lag.

options.text: Skip fan-out for authors above a follower threshold and merge their recent posts into followers' feeds at read time.
options.explanation: The hybrid keeps precomputed feeds for normal authors. Celebrity posts live in a small replicated cache and are merged when a follower reads, avoiding 120 million feed writes for one post.
